jobs.title: Marketing Intern (B2C) at Fastflo
jobs.description: Employer: Fastflo Expires: 10/16/2026 Marketing Intern, B2C Growth & UGCFastflo | Remote (Cambridge, MA, hybrid welcome) | Part-time or Full-time | PaidAbout FastfloFastflo is a hyper-growth B2B SaaS startup built at the Harvard Innovation Labs. We're changing how companies hire frontline workers: instead of forcing candidates through clunky web forms, applications happen natively inside WhatsApp and iMessage. Around 80% of candidates finish their application, versus roughly 15% on traditional flows. We recently closed our seed round, and we're now launching something new: a job board built for candidates.That job board needs to be everywhere candidates are. That's your job.The RoleYou will own consumer marketing for our job board launch. Not "support" it, not "assist with" it. Own it. You'll be the person responsible for getting job seekers to discover us, and you'll have real freedom in how you do it.We do things very differently at Fastflo, and that's why we win. We're not looking for someone to schedule three polished posts a week. We're looking for someone with the creative instincts and the nerve to run guerrilla plays that bigger companies would never approve: content that gets shared, stunts that get talked about, ideas that punch far above our budget.And we're not hiring for a semester. We're hiring the person who could lead marketing at Fastflo. This internship is how you earn that: prove it and the intention is to convert you into a long-term position with real ownership of the function as we scale.What You'll DoCreate UGC yourself: short-form video for TikTok, Reels, and Shorts about job searching, careers, and our job boardBuild a machine for getting others to create UGC: creator partnerships, campus ambassadors, challenges, whatever worksRun our candidate-facing social channels and grow them from scratchInvent and execute guerrilla campaigns to drive job seekers to the boardTrack what's working and double down ruthlesslyWhat Success Looks LikeJob seekers discovering and signing up for the job board. You'll have clear growth targets, full ownership of the channels, and a direct line to the founders. When your video hits, everyone will know it was yours.Who Thrives HereCurrently pursuing or recently completed a bachelor's or master's degreeYou already make content, or you've been itching for an excuse to startA ton of initiative: you generate ideas without being asked and ship them without hand-holdingComfortable on camera, or great at getting other people to beScrappy: you see a $0 budget as a creative constraint, not an obstacleNo formal marketing experience required. Taste, energy, and output matter more.Compensation & LogisticsPaid position with performance incentives tied to growth resultsAcademic credit available where your program allows, in addition to compensationRemote by default; you're welcome to join us in person or hybrid in Cambridge if you're localPart-time or full-time depending on your availabilityThis role is designed to convert: perform well and you move into a long-term position with a path to leading marketing at Fastflo

jobs.feedName: David Nazarian College of Business & Economics
jobs.title: 2027 Summer Associate (Intern) at BRG
jobs.description: Employer: BRG Expires: 10/17/2026 We Do Consulting Differently Berkeley Research Group (BRG) is a global consulting firm that helps its clients, which consist of leading organizations and businesses, advance in three key areas: disputes and investigations, corporate finance, and performance improvement and advisory. We are an integrated group of experts, industry leaders, academics, data scientists, and economists, working beyond borders and disciplines. We harness our collective expertise to deliver the inspired insights and practical strategies our clients need to stay ahead of what’s next. About the Role The work of a Summer Associate can have quantitative and qualitative aspects, depending on the needs of specific projects and the Summer Associate’s skills and interests. Projects range from subject matter research to data collection, to the preparation of economic, statistical, financial, and other forms of analysis. You will build technical skills and contribute to work that shapes important legal and business outcomes. The Summer Associate program will be approximately 8 weeks long and begin in Summer 2027. We’re committed to helping our Summer Associates succeed by providing them with dedicated mentors, training programs, hands-on learning opportunities and support from industry experts. Our Summer Associate program is a pipeline program, and we aim to convert Summer Associates to full-time Associates after graduation, assuming the role is a fit on both ends. What You’ll Do Develop a practical understanding of industries, markets, legal claims, and business issues relevant to each engagement by gathering and reviewing information from our clients and their business, academic literature, legal documents, specialized industry resources, commercial databases, or other sources appropriate for the unique requirements of a project. Identify, collect, develop, maintain, analyze and review data, qualitative materials, spreadsheets and other files as dictated by complex project needs. Combine programming, model building, and statistical analysis skills using relational database and statistical programs to analyze a variety of subjects with software such as SQL, R, Stata, SAS, Python, or Snowflake. Interact with senior staff, experts, and clients to clearly communicate questions, findings, economic and business concepts, and recommendations. Demonstrate creativity and efficient analytical skills to develop novel solutions tailored to unique projects. Provide valuable contributions to client deliverables and expert reports. Qualifications Progression towards a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Economics, Mathematics, Data Science, Statistics, Accounting, Business, Finance, Healthcare Administration or a related analytical field, with an expected graduation date between Winter 2027 and Summer 2028.3.6 GPA or higher preferred. Demonstrated interest in applying analytics to business, financial, legal, regulatory, or policy questions. Strong quantitative, research, problem-solving, and written communication skills. Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced, client-service environment. Attention to detail, intellectual curiosity, and a commitment to producing high-quality work. Experience with statistical, econometric and programming tools such as Excel, Stata, R, Python, SQL or similar platforms is preferred. Fluency with AI tools is desirable. Candidates must be able to submit verification of their legal right to work in the United States, without company sponsorship now or in the future. Our Practice Areas Summer Associates are hired to support project work aligned to one of BRG’s practice areas, though there may be flexibility to work across multiple practice areas. Candidates can select a preferred practice area as part of the application process. You can find more information about them below. 1. Antitrust & Competition: Experts in our antitrust practice apply learning from industrial organization, econometrics and microeconomic theory to provide testimony to counsel, corporations, and governments in matters involving antitrust litigation and merger reviews. Our experts and academic affiliates have testified in some of the largest and most significant antitrust matters of the past two decades, including antitrust actions involving platforms and multi-sided markets, automobile manufacturers, insurance companies, financial markets (e.g., LIBOR and foreign exchange) and other industries. Our project teams frequently evaluate industry conduct and assess antitrust liability, calculate damages from anticompetitive conduct and build simulation models to understand the impacts of proposed mergers. 2. Business Insurance Claims (BIC): We provide immediate and strategic guidance to policyholders following a catastrophe. Our BIC experts meticulously analyze financial data and operational records, develop robust financial models, and prepare comprehensive, well-documented insurance claims, accelerating resolution and maximizing claim payments. 3. Construction: We specialize in data analytics, litigation support, claims/dispute analysis, scheduling/logistics management and expert witness testimony within the construction, engineering, and architectural fields. Our team supports clients through budget and payment advisory, loss assessment and valuation, estimations and takeoffs, and insurance and damages claim valuations. We also specialize in providing our clients with budgetary and payment oversight, project management recommendations, project scheduling generation, and constructability and viability analyses for both upcoming and ongoing construction projects. 4. Commercial Disputes: We combine exceptional analytical and accounting skills and industry-specific knowledge to provide comprehensive support throughout the legal process. From initial case assessment and in-depth damages analysis to litigation support and expert testimony in hearings, trials, arbitration, regulatory proceedings, and mediation, we deliver data-driven insights to secure favorable outcomes. 5. Consumer Protection, Product Liability & Environment: Our experts are regularly engaged in matters involving claims of consumer fraud, product liability, false advertising, data privacy and data breach, and alleged violations of environmental and natural resource law. Associates in this area employ techniques from microeconomic theory, econometrics, marketing and environmental and resource economics to address in class certification, liability and damages. 6. Energy & Climate: We help clients across the global energy value chain address complex strategic, commercial, financial, market, regulatory, and dispute-related issues. Our work spans power and utilities, oil and gas, renewables, storage, advanced nuclear, eMobility, hydrogen and low-carbon fuels, carbon management, infrastructure, and the broader energy transition. We conduct rigorous market research, economic modeling, and detailed reporting, helping clients address legal and business challenges. 7. Financial Institutions Advisory: We are a trusted advisor to leading financial services companies. We work to help clients meet and execute strategies related to risk and regulation, compliance, financial crime, innovations in technology, accounting, cryptocurrency and blockchain, business process outsourcing, the Bank Secrecy Act, anti-money laundering, lookbacks, data quality, and evolving customer experience expectations. 8. Healthcare Advisory: As healthcare organizations navigate increasing reimbursement pressure, workforce challenges, regulatory and enforcement complexity, and rapid technological change, we work alongside executive teams and governing bodies to identify opportunities, implement practical solutions, and deliver measurable, lasting results. Our integrated team combines deep industry expertise across strategy, revenue management, operational excellence, clinical transformation, and technology and AI with the comprehensive capabilities of a global advisory firm and the agility, senior attention, and client service of a boutique consultancy. 9. Healthcare Analytics and Disputes: We tackle complex legal and operational challenges in the healthcare industry using data-driven, objective, and innovative approaches. Our experts lead advisory, risk management, and litigation matters, combining deep healthcare industry expertise with cutting edge research, analytics and financial modeling. 10. Intellectual Property: Our intellectual property experts and academic affiliates regularly testify on damages, trademark confusion, irreparable harm and commercial success. Many of our matters require expertise in consumer behavior, judgment and decision-making and our project teams work on some of the world's largest patent infringement, trademark infringement, trade secret misappropriation, and copyright infringement cases. Associates in this practice regularly build econometric models of market prices, analyze survey data and the results of choice experiments and assist with the preparation of expert reports and other client deliverables. Locations Summer Associates will primarily be hired in locations like Boston, Washington DC, Chicago, New York, Houston, Los Angeles and the San Francisco Bay Area. There are also a limited number of opportunities in smaller offices like Tampa and Pittsburgh. Summer Associates are expected to work in the office five days per week to take full advantage of the mentorship, collaboration, and relationship-building opportunities that support their professional growth. Remote roles for practices that require frequent travel to client sites are also available. How to Apply Interested candidates should submit a copy of their resume, cover letter and transcript through the job posting. You can find the job application deadlines listed below:Deadline for priority review: September 5Deadline for secondary review: September 19Deadline for final review: October 16 When applying, please answer the questionnaire to indicate your location and practice area preferences. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. A member of the recruiting team will be in touch if there is an interest in scheduling interviews. Salary Range: $25/hour - $40/hour Global Competition Review recently recognized BRG as an Outstanding firm in GCR 100: Economics 2025, which ranks the world’s leading economic consultancies. Consulting Magazine recognized BRG as a Best Firms to Work for in 2025. BRG is a recipient of the Human Rights Campaigns Equality 100 Award for our LGBTQ+ corporate policies, practices and beliefs. About BRG BRG combines world-leading academic credentials with world-tested business expertise and purpose-built emerging technologies. Our culture centers on agility and connectivity which sets us apart and gets you ahead. At BRG, our professionals include specialist consultants, industry experts, renowned academics, and leading-edge data scientists. Together, they bring a diversity of real-world experience, data, and human and artificial intelligence, to economics, disputes, and investigations; corporate finance; and performance improvement services that address the most complex challenges facing organizations across the globe. Our unique structure nurtures the interdisciplinary relationships that give us the edge, laying the groundwork for more informed insights and more original, incisive thinking. When paired with our global reach and resources, our diverse perspectives and technical capabilities make us uniquely capable to address our clients’ challenges. We get results because we know how to apply our thinking to your world. At BRG, we don’t just show you what’s possible. We’re built to help you make it happen. BRG is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. Our hiring practices provide equal opportunity for employment without regard to race, religion, color, sex, gender, national origin, age, United States military veteran status, ancestry, sexual orientation, marital status, family structure, medical condition including genetic characteristics or information, veteran status, or mental or physical disability so long as the essential functions of the job can be performed with or without reasonable accommodation, or any other protected category under federal, state, or local law.

jobs.title: Assistant Examiner Intern at Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond
jobs.description: Employer: Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond Expires: 10/17/2026 About the Opportunity The Richmond Fed Supervision, Regulation, and Credit (SRC) department is now hiring for our 2027 Summer Internship Program. SRC is responsible for the supervision of bank holding companies, state member banks, and foreign banking organizations. Supervision is completed from two differing aspects, safety and soundness (assessing a bank’s financial performance and risk to the FDIC insurance fund) and consumer compliance (assessing a bank’s compliance with consumer guidelines such as Fair Lending and Community Reinvestment Act). SRC is also responsible for Discount Window operations where money can be lent to organizations in need of funding. The Assistant Examiner Internship Program provides a unique experience to explore SRC’s supervision business lines and will be located in Richmond, VA. The program provides summer interns with the opportunity to enhance essential business skills and increase understanding of the Federal Reserve’s role in the supervision of financial institutions. During the program, you will gain exposure to the supervisory process through bank examination participation. While participating on bank examinations, you will interact with management at supervised institutions, review reports, participate in meetings, and assess risk exposures. You may review topics ranging from adequacy of risk management practices, operational controls, financial condition, and/or compliance with banking laws and regulations. In addition, you will participate in foundational learning, develop a relationship with a mentor, create and deliver presentations, and complete a final project As part of the Bank’s larger intern cohort, you will participate in professional development activities and be provided with an extensive understanding of the work of the Federal Reserve. In addition to specific business area tasks, you will receive leadership training, mentorship and valuable networking opportunities. What You Will Do: Rotate through three supervision business lines. Participate in an examination at the Federal Reserve Bank and/or a state member bank. Communicate findings and conclusions of supervisory activities to examination staff and senior management. Responsibly handle highly sensitive and confidential information. Observe and participate in relevant meetings to gain an extensive overview of the department and critical examination issues. Participate in a bank simulation exercise. Work with other interns to create and deliver a presentation to SRC related to internship experience. Qualifications: Rising senior with a minimum 3.3 GPA with a preferred emphasis in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, Economics, Mathematics, Statistics, or related field. Strong project management skills, including organization, planning and execution, analytical and problem-solving skills. Strong communication and interpersonal skills, including the ability to work effectively in a team environment. Intellectual curiosity with willingness to ask questions. Other Requirements and Considerations: An applicant posting for employment as a Federal Reserve examiner intern must be a U.S. citizen or hold a permanent residence visa/Green Card and be an intending citizen. Sponsorship or practical training extensions are not available for this position. Under conflicts of interest guidelines administered by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, examining personnel may not participate on an examination of a financial institution or affiliate if the examiner was employed by the financial institution or affiliate within the past 12 months. Please review the Bank’s Code of Conduct to ensure compliance with conflicts of interest rules and personal investment restrictions. The Code is available on the About Us, Careers webpage at www.richmondfed.org. FRB ethics rules generally prohibit employees and their immediate families from owning investments in banks, savings associations or their holding companies (Section 5.3). Additionally, employees engaged in Supervision and Regulation may be subject to borrowing and deposit restrictions. These employees may need to recuse themselves from certain supervisory work based on: their borrowing relationships if a financial institution employs a member of the employee’s immediate family if the individual was employed by the financial institution or affiliate within the past 12 months In certain cases, the recusal may be so extensive it could materially reduce the effectiveness of the prospective employee. Selected candidate is subject to special background check procedures. The hourly rate for summer interns is $23.50/hour. jobs.feedName: David Nazarian College of Business & Economics
jobs.title: AI/ Machine Learning Engineering Intern at Gecko Robotics, Inc.
jobs.description: Employer: Gecko Robotics, Inc. Expires: 10/17/2026 Gecko Robotics is seeking an AI/ML Engineering Intern to join our Engineering team in New York for Summer 2027. This is a full-time, onsite internship, Monday through Friday.Gecko collects some of the richest inspection data in the world: ultrasonic and other non-destructive testing (NDT) measurements from wall-climbing robots, paired with the documents, drawings, and operational records that describe the assets they inspect. You will work on a defined project that turns that data into decisions, building models and the systems around them that run reliably on real customer data. This is an engineering internship, not an analytics one. We build the systems that analyze the data, not just the analysis.Due to government program requirements, candidates must be authorized to work in the United States.What you will doOwn a scoped machine learning project from problem framing through evaluation and integration, under the guidance of experienced engineers.Build data pipelines in Python that clean, label, and structure NDT sensor data, documents, or operational records for model training and inference.Train, evaluate, and iterate on models, and design evaluations that reflect how the output will be used in the field.Integrate a model or LLM-based workflow into a service or tool that other engineers and Forward Deployment Engineers can use.Investigate failure modes on messy, real-world data, document what you find, and recommend what to fix next.Use version control, code review, testing, and experiment tracking to produce work others can reproduce and build on.Present your project, results, and recommended next steps at the end of the internship.Technologies We UsePython, PyTorch or similar ML frameworks, NumPy and pandas, SQL, LLM APIs and agent frameworks, Git, Linux, and cloud infrastructure (GCP). Depending on the project, you may also work with signal-processing tools for ultrasonic data, document-processing and information-extraction pipelines, or orchestration tools such as Airflow. The specific tools will depend on the assigned project. About YouYou are an engineer who happens to work in machine learning. You care whether a model works on real data, not just on a benchmark, and you are comfortable owning the code around the model: the pipeline, the evaluation, and the integration. You approach new problems methodically, communicate clearly about results and uncertainty, and are excited to be the first person to look at a problem. Required SkillsCurrently pursuing a bachelor’s, master’s, or doctoral degree in computer science, electrical engineering, applied mathematics, physics, or a related technical discipline, with an expected graduation date between December 2027 and May 2028.Ability to work onsite in New York, Monday through Friday, for the full Summer 2027 internship.Strong programming experience in Python, including writing well-structured, tested code beyond notebooks.Coursework or project experience in machine learning, including training and evaluating models on real datasets.Working understanding of linear algebra, probability, and statistics.Working familiarity with Git or similar version control systems.Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain results, quantify uncertainty, and collaborate on ambiguous problems.Ability to independently close knowledge gaps, stay organized, and learn from feedback. Preferred SkillsGraduate-level coursework or research in machine learning, signal processing, or computer vision.Experience taking a model beyond a notebook: building a pipeline, an API, or a tool around it.Experience with LLM APIs, retrieval, information extraction, or document understanding.Experience with time-series or sensor data, especially ultrasonic, acoustic, or other physical measurements.Exposure to cloud infrastructure, preferably GCP, and to containers such as Docker.Interest in industrial, defense, or infrastructure applications where reliability matters.

jobs.description: Employer: The Wine Group Expires: 10/17/2026 Under the supervision of the Winemaker, Intern Winemaking duties will vary with the intent to participate in the overall wine quality from grape to finished product while following sustainable TWG practices. jobs.description: Employer: Baystate Financial Expires: 10/18/2026 BEGIN YOUR FINANCIAL CAREER WITH AN INTERNSHIP WITH BAYSTATE FINANCIAL **We are currently interviewing for our Summer 2027 internship class in all of our New England offices** The first step in our interview process is to join a group information session via Zoom to learn more about Baystate Financial, the career of an advisor, and the industry in general. Our next information session is scheduled for Tuesday, October 20th at 11am. Please use the following link to register: https://financialguide.zoom.us/meeting/register/u6pqVizjStCHPfR_jwynsw In addition, please complete the Culture Index Survey listed below:https://go.cultureindex.com/p/3Cs6YkulwTG1 Baystate Financial is selecting full-time college students for our hands-on internship program. We are seeking highly motivated, entrepreneurial students, interested in a career in finance. Selected candidates will be given the opportunity to get fully licensed as a financial advisor, receive top-notch training and mentorship, and gain valuable professional experience transferable to any industry. Interns that prove to be an asset to the firm will be offered a full-time position upon graduating. Financial Advisor Interns are taught how to build a financial services practice from the ground up. jobs.title: 2027 Summer Intern, Pricing Associate (Reston, VA or Remote) at ICF
jobs.description: Employer: ICF Expires: 10/18/2026 ICF is seeking a motivated and detail-oriented Pricing Associate Intern to join our Corporate Pricing Team. In this role, you’ll learn to develop accurate, compliant, and competitive pricing solutions that support ICF’s proposals and contribute to meaningful client outcomes. You will work with members of the pricing department, operations teams, capture managers, contracts, finance, and proposal professionals to analyze solicitation requirements, support and build pricing models, and help prepare cost and business proposals for federal, state, local, and commercial clients. Our summer internship is full-time for 10-weeks beginning in early June and ending in early August. Work may be hybrid from Reston, VA or performed from any U.S. location. At this time, we are unable to provide relocation nor housing assistance. This is a strong opportunity for a candidate who is interested in growing in pricing, finance, cost analysis, and government contracting. You’ll gain exposure to the full proposal lifecycle, learn from experienced pricing professionals, and build skills in financial analysis, compliance, collaboration, and business strategy. The successful candidate will bring strong analytical skills, intellectual curiosity, a collaborative mindset, and a commitment to accuracy and continuous improvement. Key Responsibilities Support the development of timely, accurate, and compliant cost and business proposals that help ICF compete effectively and deliver strong value to clients. Review requests for proposals and related documents to identify pricing requirements, evaluation criteria, submission instructions, compliance considerations, and key assumptions. Assist in building, maintaining, and quality-checking pricing models, including labor, other direct costs, travel, subcontractor costs, indirect rates, fees, and escalation assumptions. Collect, organize, and analyze cost inputs from operations, subcontractors, finance, contracts, and other stakeholders to support complete, clear, and defensible pricing submissions. Document pricing assumptions, methodologies, and supporting rationale so proposal teams and reviewers can easily understand how pricing aligns with the proposed technical approach. Participate in pricing strategy discussions, proposal reviews, color team reviews, and internal approval processes by preparing analyses and responding to reviewer feedback. Prepare financial analyses, scenario comparisons, and pricing summaries that help proposal teams evaluate competitiveness, profitability, and risk. Contribute ideas to improve pricing templates, tools, quality controls, and processes that support consistency, compliance, and efficiency across proposals. Basic Qualifications By start date at least 15 completed credit hours in Accounting, Data Analytics, Economics, Finance, Management, Supply Chain Management or related field. Preferred Qualifications Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, including formulas, data organization, workbook review, and the ability to learn and work with detailed pricing models. Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work accurately with financial, operational, and proposal data. Clear written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to summarize assumptions, analyses, and recommendations for different audiences. Attention to detail, sound judgment, and the ability to follow structured processes and meet deadlines. Interest in cost estimation, pricing, financial analysis, business operations, government consulting, or government contracting.

jobs.title: Financial Advisor Intern at Baystate Financial
jobs.description: Employer: Baystate Financial Expires: 10/18/2026 BEGIN YOUR FINANCIAL CAREER WITH AN INTERNSHIP WITH BAYSTATE FINANCIAL **We are currently interviewing for our Summer 2027 internship class in all of our New England offices** The first step in our interview process is to join a group information session via Zoom to learn more about Baystate Financial, the career of an advisor, and the industry in general. Our next information session is scheduled for Tuesday, October 20th at 11am. Please use the following link to register: https://financialguide.zoom.us/meeting/register/u6pqVizjStCHPfR_jwynsw In addition, please complete the Culture Index Survey listed below:https://go.cultureindex.com/p/3Cs6YkulwTG1 Baystate Financial is selecting full-time college students for our hands-on internship program. We are seeking highly motivated, entrepreneurial students, interested in a career in finance. Selected candidates will be given the opportunity to get fully licensed as a financial advisor, receive top-notch training and mentorship, and gain valuable professional experience transferable to any industry. Interns that prove to be an asset to the firm will be offered a full-time position upon graduating. About This Internship Right from the beginning students are given the resources needed to help clients achieve financial security. Financial Advisor Interns are taught how to build a financial services practice from the ground up. With the help of senior advisors and the Baystate team, students will meet with clients to learn more about their individual definition of financial security and develop a “financial roadmap” to get them from where they are currently, to where they want to be. At the end of the internship, successful interns will be able to exhibit: An Understanding of How to Create and Implement a Personal Financial Plan Client Acquisition and Marketing Strategies The Role of a Full Time Financial Advisor Exceptional Listening and Problem-Solving Skills The Ability to Work Well in Both a Team and Individual Capacity Candidate Characteristics Although there are a wide variety of college majors, personal backgrounds, and life experiences that will see success in this role, there are a few characteristics we see exhibited in the majority of our most successful interns: Strong Desire to Help People, Including Individuals, Families, and Small Businesses Motivated to Work in a Client Facing/ Sales/ Finance Role Competitive, with an Entrepreneurial Spirit and a Vision to Build and Grow Their Own Business High Standards or Integrity, Empathy, Competency, Work Ethic, and Professionalism “Interested individuals are invited to apply. And, while we appreciate every applicant's interest, only those under consideration will be contacted.” About Baystate Financial Since its founding in 1901, Baystate Financial has provided comprehensive financial services, life and disability insurance, estate planning, business succession planning, retirement funding, education funding strategies, and investment management to a diverse client base. More than a century of providing guidance, insight, and results has made Baystate Financial one of the oldest and largest wealth management firms in the northeast, with 12 offices in 6 New England States. Baystate Financial is comprised of a team of over 300 advisors and over 400 support staff, many of whom contribute to building financial plans for a wide variety of individuals and businesses. Baystate Financials’ strategy is tailored to help fulfill their client’s individual goals, with the understanding that every client’s goals are different.

jobs.feedName: David Nazarian College of Business & Economics
jobs.title: 2027 Summer Intern, Contracts Administration (Reston, VA) at ICF
jobs.description: Employer: ICF Expires: 10/18/2026 2027 Summer Intern, Contracts Administration At ICF, we work on projects that have an impact on real people. From ensuring families have a house that will survive the next hurricane, to helping curb teen vaping, to keeping our nation safe from cybersecurity threats, and more - ICFers are changemakers who do work with purpose. We are currently hiring interns to join our Contracts, Procurement and Pricing (CPP) teams (Contracts, Subcontracts, Purchasing, and Compliance). This group is part of the internal support process within ICF, helping the project teams win and manage their projects. We help shape policy and procedures to comply with government, commercial, state, and local practices to ensure we remain compliant with our client guidelines. Some of ICF’s major clients include Federal Highway Administration, Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), Exelon Utilities, LA Metro, Centers for Disease Control (CDC), Army Research Institute and Puerto Rico Dept of Housing. This is a full-time, 10-week, entry level internship position that begins in June and ends in August 2027. The internship will work a hybrid schedule from our Reston, VA office (2x per week). At this time, we are unable to provide relocation nor housing assistance. Pay is $23 per hour. As a Contracts Intern, you will provide direct support to the ICF Contract Administration (CA) Team by: Assisting with the review of Non-Disclosure and Teaming Agreements for future business opportunities where ICF will be a subcontractor. Assisting with the management of contract files on the Contracts’ SharePoint site (e.g., naming, reorganizing, uploading documents, identifying documents by type and tagging them). Assisting with contract set-ups in our Contract Management System. Assisting with internal data calls and internal audits. You will gain valuable experience in the proposal development process from the CA’s point of view to include: Reviewing solicitation terms and conditions (RFPs, etc.) Assisting with the business/price volume response to include: compliance review, writing the price narrative, and completing required forms/certifications. Coordination with the proposal response team, including Pricing, Subcontracts, Proposal Coordinators, et al., including attending formal proposal review meetings. As a Subcontracts Administration Intern, you will provide direct support to the Subcontracts Administration Team by: Assisting with the drafting of Non-Disclosure Agreements (NDAs), Teaming Agreements, and modifications to existing agreements related to future business opportunities where ICF may engage companies or independent consultants as subcontractors or partners. Supporting vendor setup and maintaining subcontract records in SharePoint to help ensure the accuracy and completeness of subcontract compliance files. Using Microsoft Copilot and other approved productivity tools, as appropriate, to assist with summarizing solicitation or agreement requirements, organizing compliance information, and improving the efficiency and quality of administrative work products, subject to review and approval by the Subcontracts Administration Team. Assisting with the preparation of subcontractor Requests for Proposals (RFPs) and Requests for Quotations (RFQs) for distribution to external vendors, consultants, or teaming partners. You will gain valuable experience in subcontract management and proposal development from the perspective of Subcontracts Administration, including: Reviewing Requests for Proposals (RFPs), Requests for Quotations (RFQs), and related solicitation documents to identify subcontract requirements, terms, and conditions. Coordinating with proposal response teams, including Pricing, Contracts, Proposal Coordinators, and other stakeholders, by attending formal proposal and subcontract review meetings. Supporting communications with potential and existing subcontractors regarding documentation, compliance requirements, and related administrative needs. As a Purchasing Intern, you will provide direct support to the ICF Purchasing Team by: Assisting with the review, drafting, and negotiation of Non-Disclosure Agreements (NDAs), Master Services Agreements (MSAs), Software as a Service (SaaS) and other software subscription agreements, Statements of Work (SOWs), and Purchase Orders (POs). Supporting procurement file compliance activities, including preparing procurement award summaries, price analyses, and contract documentation. Conducting market and supplier research to support sourcing and procurement strategies. Serving as a liaison between suppliers and internal business units to address purchasing inquiries, explain purchasing processes, and assist with issue resolution. Assisting with supplier onboarding, contract administration, and procurement-related reporting and data analysis. Supporting internal spend analysis, data reconciliation, and process improvement initiatives. You will gain exposure to the sourcing and proposal process from a Buyer’s perspective, including: Preparing and distributing Requests for Proposal (RFPs), Requests for Quotations (RFQs), and Requests for Information (RFIs). Participating in supplier sourcing and competitive evaluation activities. Reviewing supplier proposals for completeness, responsiveness, and compliance with procurement requirements. Supporting supplier negotiations and contract award activities. Assisting with supplier performance and risk assessments. As a Compliance Intern, you will focus on supporting policy, reporting, and data analysis efforts that support the Contracts, Procurement, and Pricing team as well as other ICF stakeholders. Duties may include: Creating new AI bots and job aids for purchasing system compliance topics and contracts compliance guidance Researching state and local regulations and requirements for comparison with federal law Tracking and updating clause matrices for U.S. Government regulations Assisting in data analysis and reporting for small business utilization, prime contract data, etc. Individuals with a focus-area preference (Contracts, Subcontracts, Purchasing, and/or Compliance) should note such on their cover letter or resume, otherwise, applicants may be considered for any of the above teams. Basic Qualification: At least 30 credit hours of college coursework completed by start date. U.S. Citizenship is required per Federal contracts Preferred Qualifications: College studies in Accounting, Business Administration, Communications, Data Analysis, Economics, Management, Marketing, Psychology, Project Management, Public Policy, Supply Chain Management & Logistics or other related field. Interest in government contracting and procurement, research analysis, negotiating, business administration and government consulting. Strong interpersonal and organizational skills. Strong attention to detail. Strong communication skills (written/verbal). Strong computer skills (Microsoft).
